title: Farah's bakery outgrows its form
body: Farah started baking cakes and cookies in her home kitchen as a sole proprietor. Within six years her bakery has grown into four outlets in her city. She still personally handles purchasing, accounts, staff and customer complaints, and she often feels stretched. A supermarket chain has now offered her a contract to supply packaged cookies to its stores across the country. Accepting it would require a factory, modern machinery and a large amount of capital, far more than her savings and bank loans can provide. Her bank manager has also warned her that if the expanded business fails, creditors could claim her house and car. Her uncle advises her to bring in a partner, while her accountant suggests forming a company and inviting investors. Farah wants the business to outlive her and to be run by experts in production, finance and marketing.
